name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
captions: Seoul's grandest palace, framed by Bugaksan mountain. Rent a hanbok nearby and you can walk in for free.
Built in 1395, Gyeongbokgung still sets the rhythm of downtown Seoul. Catch the royal guard changing ceremony at Gwanghwamun Gate.
Wide courtyards, painted eaves and a mountain backdrop. Go early on a weekday for the quietest walk through the palace.
Every gate opens onto another courtyard. Which corner of Gyeongbokgung would you explore first?

name: Changdeokgung & Changgyeonggung
captions: Changdeokgung follows the hills instead of flattening them, part of why it's a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The Secret Garden behind Changdeokgung is only open on guided tours, so book ahead if it's on your list.
Next door, Changgyeonggung's old glasshouse and pond make a calm detour from the city.
Two neighboring palaces, one long afternoon. Come in autumn, when these courtyards turn gold. 🍂

name: Deoksugung & Jeongdong
captions: A traditional palace and a European-style stone hall side by side, right in the middle of the city.
Walk the stone-wall road along Deoksugung, one of Seoul's favorite strolls in every season.
Deoksugung stays open into the evening, when the lights come on and City Hall glows next door.
Jeongdong's quiet lanes still hold churches and legation buildings from over a century ago.

name: Bukchon Hanok Village
captions: Hundreds of hanok houses packed between two royal palaces. People live here, so keep voices low as you wander.
Tiled rooftops all the way to the downtown skyline. Bukchon looks best from its uphill lanes.
Wooden gates, stone walls and quiet alleys. Visiting hours are limited in the busiest lanes, so plan a daytime walk.
Old Seoul, still lived in. Which alley would you get lost in first?

name: Seochon
captions: West of Gyeongbokgung, Seochon trades crowds for small galleries, bookshops and hanok cafés.
At Tongin Market, swap old-style brass coins for a lunchbox filled with market snacks.
Follow the lanes uphill to Suseong-dong Valley, where Inwangsan's rocks meet the city.
Seochon is where locals go when Bukchon feels too busy. Slow mornings, good coffee, quiet alleys. ☕

name: Ikseon-dong & Insadong
captions: Ikseon-dong packs a hundred-year-old hanok neighborhood with cafés, bakeries and tiny restaurants.
Insadong is the place for traditional tea, hanji paper and handmade crafts.
Ssamziegil's spiral walkway climbs past small craft shops. Start at the bottom and keep going up.
Narrow alleys, warm lights and the smell of street snacks. Best explored on an empty stomach.

name: Namsan & N Seoul Tower
captions: N Seoul Tower sits in the middle of the city, so you can spot it from almost anywhere in Seoul.
Walk up the trails or ride the cable car. Either way, the view from the top is worth it.
Love locks, city lights and the whole skyline in one turn of the head.
Namsan is a forest in the middle of downtown, with walking trails far quieter than the streets below.

name: Han River
captions: Seoul's favorite way to unwind: a mat on the grass, fried chicken and the Han River at sunset.
Dozens of bridges cross the Han, and every riverside park has its own view of them.
In the warmer months, Banpo Bridge's rainbow fountain lights up the river after dark. 🌈
Rent a bike and follow the river paths. They run for kilometers along both banks.

name: Seongsu & Seoul Forest
captions: Old factories and warehouses turned into cafés, studios and pop-up stores. Seongsu is Seoul's creative corner.
Seoul Forest is right next door for a green break between café stops.
Brick buildings, queues for the newest pop-up and great coffee. Seongsu seems to change every month.
Come for the cafés, stay for the side streets. What would you check out first in Seongsu?

name: Dongdaemun & DDP
captions: Dongdaemun Design Plaza's silver curves were designed by Zaha Hadid, and they look different from every angle.
Old and new side by side: Heunginjimun Gate has stood a short walk from DDP for centuries.
Dongdaemun stays busy late, with fashion malls and street food going long after dark.
Futuristic curves by day, glowing lights by night. DDP is a different place after sunset.

name: Lotte World Tower & Seokchon Lake
captions: At 555 meters, Lotte World Tower is Korea's tallest building, and its observatory looks straight down on the city.
Seokchon Lake wraps around the tower's base, and in spring its paths turn pink with cherry blossoms. 🌸
A lakeside walk with Korea's tallest tower as the backdrop. Sunset is the time to go.
From the lake path to the 123rd floor, Jamsil does skyline views like nowhere else in Seoul.

name: Gwanghwamun & Cheonggyecheon
captions: Gwanghwamun Square links the palace gate to the statues of King Sejong and Admiral Yi Sun-sin.
Cheonggyecheon runs below street level through downtown. Follow it for a quiet walk in the middle of the city.
This is the heart of old Seoul: palace gates, a wide plaza and mountains beyond.
Step down from the traffic to Cheonggyecheon, where stepping stones and lights line the stream.

name: Hongdae, Yeonnam & Mangwon
captions: Buskers, indie music and late-night energy. Hongdae is where Seoul's young creative scene hangs out.
Gyeongui Line Forest Park turns an old railway into a long green strip through Yeonnam-dong.
Mangwon Market is a local favorite for cheap street food and a slower pace.
Murals, vintage shops and tiny bars. Which part of Hongdae would you start with?

name: Itaewon & Hannam
captions: Itaewon and Hannam mix food from around the world with design shops and galleries.
Climb the hilly side streets for rooftop views and some of Seoul's most international menus.
Hannam-dong's quiet lanes hide concept stores, cafés and the Leeum Museum of Art.
One neighborhood, a dozen cuisines. Itaewon is where Seoul goes out to eat.

name: Myeongdong & Namdaemun
captions: Myeongdong's main streets fill with food stalls in the evening, so bring an appetite.
Skincare shops, street snacks and neon signs on one of Seoul's busiest shopping streets.
Sungnyemun, Seoul's old south gate, stands next to Namdaemun Market, which has been trading for over 600 years.
From the cathedral on the hill to the stalls below, Myeongdong packs a lot into a few blocks.

name: Naksan Park & Seoul City Wall
captions: The Seoul City Wall runs along Naksan's ridge, and its trail is one of the best sunset walks in the city.
Ihwa Village's stairs and murals lead up to Naksan Park, with old Seoul spread out below.
Six-hundred-year-old stones and city lights after dark. On Naksan, the walls of old Seoul meet the new.
A short climb from Dongdaemun, Naksan Park gives you a wide-open view without a mountain hike.

name: COEX & Bongeunsa
captions: Starfield Library's towering shelves sit inside COEX Mall, and they're free to wander. 📚
Right across the street from COEX, Bongeunsa Temple is a calm counterpoint to Gangnam's towers.
Glass towers and a temple more than a thousand years old, facing each other across one street.
Gangnam is more than shopping: temple bells, giant bookshelves and wide boulevards in one walk.

name: Bukhansan & Inwangsan
captions: Seoul is a mountain city, and Bukhansan National Park sits right on its northern edge.
Inwangsan's rocky trail is short and steep, and it ends with one of the best views over downtown.
Granite peaks, pine trees and the whole city below. Some of Seoul's best hikes start near a subway station.
Bring water and good shoes. Seoul's mountain trails are steeper than they look. ⛰️
